variant.stem_override: A 58-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history presents to clinic with 3 months of exertional chest pressure that occurs reproducibly after walking 2–3 blocks and resolves within 5 minutes of rest. Symptoms have been stable in frequency and severity. Vital signs: BP 134/82 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98%. Cardiac exam is unremarkable. Resting ECG is normal sinus rhythm with no ST or T-wave abnormalities. Recent routine labs reveal a TSH of 2.1 mIU/L (normal range 0.4–4.0 mIU/L). He is able to exercise on a treadmill without limitation from non-cardiac comorbidities.
variant.rationale_for_variant: A single incidental finding—a normal TSH of 2.1 mIU/L—was inserted to serve as a distractor. A normal TSH confirms euthyroid status, which neither supports nor refutes obstructive CAD, does not suggest an alternative diagnosis (e.g., hyperthyroid-related angina), and does not alter any guideline-based testing pathway. All clinical features supporting an exercise treadmill ECG stress test as the correct initial diagnostic test remain entirely unchanged.
